draft.title: Appropriation and transformation
card: a later writer takes an earlier text and reshapes it for a new context. The new text stays linked to the original, but it is not a copy.
the changes the writer makes. They can alter the setting, the form or the point of view, such as telling a story through a minor character.
Each change is a choice. A new setting can move a familiar story to a different time or place. A new point of view can give a voice to someone the original left silent.
Comparing what stayed the same with what changed can show how the values of the two contexts differ. The changes show what the later writer wants to question or update.
draft.remember: Look at what a later writer changed, then ask what the change shows about shifting values.

a.q: What is the main purpose of transformation in an appropriated text?
opts: To reshape the earlier text for a new context
To copy the earlier text as closely as possible
To summarise the earlier text in fewer words
To prove the earlier text was written badly
a.why: Transformation is the set of changes that reshape an earlier text for a new context. Copying closely is wrong because an appropriation is not a copy: it changes setting, form or point of view.
a.clue: The new text is linked to the original but is not a copy.

b.q: A writer retells an old tale about a feared outcast. The new version is told by the outcast and shows the villagers as cruel. What does this change most likely reveal?
opts: Values have shifted towards sympathy for outsiders
The writer could not remember the original plot
The villagers are the same as in the old tale
The original tale was set in a different country
b.why: Changing the point of view gives the outcast a voice, so the changes suggest the later context values the outsider's side. The claim that the villagers are the same is wrong because the retelling changed how they are shown.
b.clue: Ask what the change of narrator invites a reader to feel.

a.best: To reshape the earlier text for a new context

b.best: Values have shifted towards sympathy for outsiders

problems.detail: The distractors (proving the original was written badly, summarising it) are implausible, so the question is too easy for Year 12 HSC students. The right option also repeats the card's definition word for word.

a.q: A student studies a modern novel that retells a Victorian story. Which approach best shows what the transformation reveals?
opts: Link each change to a difference between the two contexts
List the plot events the two texts have in common
Judge which of the two texts tells the better story
Read the modern novel on its own, apart from its source
a.why: Transformation means the changes, and each change is a choice that can point to a shift in values between the two contexts. Listing shared plot events is tempting, but it only shows what stayed the same, not what the changes reveal.
a.clue: The meaning lies in the changes, read against each context.
